text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Accountancy group KPMG attempts to take over accounting firm VB Groep. (p1)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm tempers euphoria over 1998 four billion guilder windfall. (p1)
- Lovers Rail is to compete with Dutch Railways (NS) on two new routes next year. (p1)
- Utility companies still in the dark about the cause of last week's power cut that hit large part of the country. (p1)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM's decision to halt transport of radio-active material affects thousands of hospitals. (p1)
- Receivers of bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker collect Dfl 109 million for creditors by continuing activities during receivership. (p2)
- Growing number of employees in the Netherlands have a company pension. (p2)
- KLM mulls the possibility of selling its 19.5 pct stake in U.S. partner Northwest Airlines. (p1)
- Central planning office (CPB) warns of unbridled growth of air traffic in the Netherlands. (p1)
- Hendrik van den Hombergh buys concrete mixer maker Mulder Boskoop after earlier misfired raid of Air Holdings. (p23)
- Securities bank KBW, a subsidiary of bank insurer Fortis, wins Reuters bourse competition. (p12)
- MPs want to hear from traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma about growth expectations for Schiphol Airport. (p3)
